newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR GETS OFF TO WINNING START.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR GETS OFF TO WINNING START.

text.p: Bruce Grobbelaar made a winning start to his new career as coach of Zimbabwe on Sunday as his team beat Tanzania 1-0 in an international friendly in Harare.
A third minute goal from captain Claudius Zviripayi decided the match, a diving header from the first corner of the game.
Grobbelaar included himself in the starting line-up but his first decision as coach was to substitute himself after 58 minutes and take up a place on the bench along with co-coach Meshack Marimo.
"I enjoyed the experience. It wasn't bad going for the first player-coach in Africa," he said afterwards.
But Grobbelaar, who plays for English second division club Plymouth Argyle, said this was not the start of a new direction in his long and chequered career.
Asked if he had aspirations of coaching in England, he answered with an emphatic "no".
He and Marimo were appointed as acting coaches for Sunday's game and Zimbabwe's African Nations' Cup qualifying match in Sudan next Saturday.
Zimbabwean officials said they were still hoping to hire a full-time coach in time for the start of the World Cup qualifiers in November.
"We have been talking to four coaches in Britain and hope to have a decision soon," Zimbabwe Football Association secretary-general Phil Hwata told Reuters.
